items.prompt: Match each body part to its sense.

figure.alt: Five pictures: an eye, an ear, a nose, a tongue and a hand for skin.

hints: Each body part goes with one sense.
Point to each part on your face and think about what it does.
Start with your eyes. What do they help you do?
items.explanation: We see with our eyes, hear with our ears, smell with our nose, taste with our tongue and feel with our skin.

items.prompt: Which sense do you use to enjoy a rainbow?
hints: Think about how you know a rainbow is there.
Which body part do you use?
Close your eyes. Can you still find the rainbow?
items.explanation: We see a rainbow with our eyes. This sense is called sight.

items.prompt: Which sense tells you a durian is near, before you see it?

options.why: You taste food in your mouth. The durian is not in your mouth yet.
A durian does not make a sound.

hints: Durian is famous for something strong.
Which body part notices things in the air?
Take a deep breath in. Which part of you is working?
items.explanation: Durian has a very strong smell. We smell it with our nose, even before we see it.

items.prompt: Which sense would you use? Sort the cards.
hints: Think about how you would notice each one.
Ask: is it a sound, or something you feel?
Start with the bell. How do you know it is ringing?
items.explanation: We hear a bell, a dog barking and thunder with our ears. We feel soft fur, a rough rock and a cold ice cube with our skin.

items.prompt: Which body part do you use to taste?

options.why: Eyes help us see colours and shapes.

hints: Think about eating your favourite food.
Which part is inside your mouth?
Picture licking an ice lolly. Which part touches it?
items.explanation: We taste with our tongue. It tells us if food is sweet, salty, sour or bitter.

items.prompt: Mangoes taste sweet. Limes taste ___.
hints: Think about the face you make when you bite a lime.
Think about the four tastes your tongue can notice.
Compare it with eating a lemon.
items.explanation: Limes taste sour. Sweet, sour, salty and bitter are tastes our tongue can notice.

items.prompt: Choose all the things you can hear.

figure.alt: Five pictures: a whistle, a rainbow, a drum, a picture book and a bird singing.

options.why: A rainbow is quiet. You see it with your eyes.
A picture book is quiet. You look at it with your eyes.

hints: Think about things that make a sound.
Imagine closing your eyes. Which ones could you still notice?
Start with the whistle. What happens when someone blows it?
items.explanation: A whistle, a drum and a bird singing all make sounds that we hear with our ears. A rainbow and a picture book are quiet.

items.prompt: Andi wants to know if a cake is sweet. Which sense should he use?

options.why: Touch tells him if the cake is soft. It cannot tell him if it is sweet.

hints: Think about how you find out if food is sweet or sour.
Which body part notices sweet, sour and salty?
Think about putting a small piece in your mouth.
items.explanation: Sweetness is a taste, so Andi uses his tongue. He should only taste food that an adult says is safe.
items.tip: Only taste things when a grown-up says they are safe to eat.

items.prompt: A smoke alarm beeps loudly. Which sense warns you?

options.why: We do not feel the beep with our skin.

hints: A beep is a sound.
Which body part notices sounds?
Cover your ears. Would the beep be harder to notice?
items.explanation: We hear the beep with our ears. Hearing can warn us about danger, like a smoke alarm or a car horn.

items.prompt: Which one can you not find out by touching?

options.why: Your skin can feel cold things.
Your fingers can feel if a stone is rough.

hints: Touch tells us about how things feel.
Ask: can my fingers feel this?
Start with the ice. Can your skin feel cold?
items.explanation: Touch tells us if things are hot, cold, rough or smooth. We need our eyes to see colours.

items.prompt: Mei holds her nose and eats a strawberry. What happens?

options.text: She cannot eat it at all.
options.why: She can still chew and swallow it.
Holding the nose makes flavours seem weaker.

hints: Smell and taste work together.
Think about eating when you have a blocked nose.
Ask: what does the nose add when we eat?
items.explanation: Our nose helps us enjoy the flavour of food. When we hold our nose, food tastes weaker than usual.

items.prompt: Draw something you can hear and something you can smell. Label them.

criteria.label: Draws something that makes a sound
Draws something that has a smell

hints: A drum or a bird makes a sound.
Flowers and food often have a smell.
items.explanation: We hear sounds with our ears and smell with our nose. A drum makes a sound and a flower has a smell.

items.prompt: Listen to the sound. Which part of your body do you use to hear it?
hints: Think about how you notice sounds.
You have two of them, one on each side of your head.
You do not hear with your eyes or your nose.
items.explanation: You hear with your ears. The speaker made a bell sound, so you use your sense of hearing.
items.listenText: Ding dong! Ding dong! The school bell is ringing.

items.prompt: We use our ___ to hear.
hints: Think about which part of your body is for hearing.
You have one on each side of your head.
It is not your eyes or your nose.
items.explanation: We hear with our ears.

items.prompt: Tap the part of the body you use to smell.

figure.alt: 5 pictures: eye, ear, nose, tongue and hand.

hints: You smell flowers and food with this part.
It is in the middle of your face.
It is not your eyes or your ears.
items.explanation: You smell with your nose.

items.prompt: Which sense do you use with each part of the body?
hints: Tap a word, then tap a picture.
You see with your eyes and hear with your ears.
You taste with your tongue.
items.explanation: You see with your eyes, hear with your ears, smell with your nose, taste with your tongue and touch with your hands.

items.prompt: What do we use our ears for?
hints: Think about music.
You do not see with your ears.
Ears help you hear.
items.explanation: We hear sounds with our ears.

items.prompt: Which sense tells you that ice is cold?

options.why: Your eyes can see ice, but they cannot feel cold.

hints: Hold ice in your hand.
Which part feels it?
The skin feels cold.
items.explanation: We feel cold with our skin. This is the sense of touch.

items.prompt: Which sense do you use to tell if a lemon is sour?

options.why: Your eyes can see a lemon, but they cannot tell if it is sour.
A lemon does not make a sound.

hints: You put it in your mouth.
The tongue helps you.
Think about eating.
items.explanation: We use our tongue to taste. Lemons taste sour.

items.prompt: Do you use your eyes or your ears? Sort the cards.
hints: Reading needs your eyes.
Listening needs your ears.
Start with the drum.
items.explanation: We use our eyes to read, see and watch. We use our ears to hear and listen.

items.prompt: Choose all the things you can smell.
hints: Use your nose.
Rainbows have no smell.
Think of the kitchen.
items.explanation: We can smell flowers, bread and soap with our nose. A rainbow is something we see. A whisper is something we hear.

items.prompt: Dimas puts his hand in a bag. Something feels soft and round. Which sense is he using?

options.why: He is not using his nose.

hints: Which part of the body is in the bag?
He feels with his skin.
Hands help us touch.
items.explanation: Dimas feels the object with his hand. He is using touch.

items.prompt: Dina has a blocked nose. Which sense is hard to use?
hints: Which part is blocked?
Nose and smell go together.
Eyes and ears still work.
items.explanation: We smell with our nose. A blocked nose makes smelling hard.

items.prompt: Match each food to its taste.
hints: Think of a sweet cake.
A lemon makes your face scrunch.
Salt is in chips.
items.explanation: Lemons are sour, sugar is sweet, salt is salty and bitter melon is bitter.

items.prompt: We use our ___ to see and our ___ to hear.
hints: Which part sees?
Which part hears?
Read the sentence slowly.
items.explanation: We see with our eyes. We hear with our ears.

items.prompt: Complete the sense table.
head: Sense
Body part
hints: Each sense has a body part.
The nose is for smell.
The tongue is in your mouth.
items.explanation: Sight uses the eyes and hearing uses the ears. Smell uses the nose and taste uses the tongue.

items.prompt: Lina walks into the kitchen. She smells something sweet. She sees a cake on the table. The cake feels soft. It tastes lovely.

parts.prompt: Which sense tells Lina the cake is soft?
What does Lina use to see the cake?

hints: Find the sentence about soft.
Which body part sees?
Skin feels soft.
items.explanation: Lina feels the soft cake with touch and sees it with her eyes.

items.prompt: Tap what you use to hear.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: eye, ear, nose and hand.

hints: Which part listens to music?
It is on the side of your head.
It starts with e.
items.explanation: We hear with our ears.

items.prompt: Tap the part you use to taste.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: ear, tongue, eye and nose.

hints: It is inside your mouth.
You lick an ice cream with it.
It is pink.
items.explanation: We taste with our tongue. It is in our mouth.

items.prompt: Which sense goes with each part? Tap a label.

figure.alt: Pictures of an eye, an ear and a nose.

hints: Match each part to a sense.
The ear is for sounds.
The nose is in the middle of the face.
items.explanation: The eye is for sight, the ear is for hearing and the nose is for smell.

items.prompt: Which sense do we use with our skin?
hints: Think about holding a cat.
Skin feels hot, cold and soft.
It starts with t.
items.explanation: Our skin helps us feel things. This is the sense of touch.

items.prompt: Draw something that tastes sweet and something that tastes sour.
hints: Think of fruits.
Cake is sweet and lemon is sour.
items.explanation: Cakes and honey taste sweet. Lemons and limes taste sour.

items.prompt: Listen. Which sense are you using?
items.listenText: Can you hear the bell ring?
hints: Listen again.
You hear with your ears.
It is not smell.
items.explanation: You listen with your ears, so you use hearing.

items.prompt: Hana is blindfolded. She holds a small, hard ball that rattles. Which senses does she use?
hints: What does a blindfold stop?
She holds the ball.
The ball rattles.
items.explanation: She feels the ball with touch and she hears the rattle. The blindfold stops sight.

items.prompt: Which thing can you not find out only by looking?
hints: Which sense do you need?
Eyes see colour and size.
Taste needs the tongue.
items.explanation: We need to taste a lemon to know its taste. We can see colour, size and shape.

items.prompt: Bayu covers his eyes and ears. Which can he still do?

options.why: He needs his eyes to read.

hints: Which parts are covered?
Which body part is free?
Smell uses the nose.
items.explanation: Bayu uses his nose to smell, so he can still smell a flower.
